title: AdWords and Generalized Online Matching
source_inventory_policy: Source basis: documented source inventory and prior source audit for Mehta-Saberi-Vazirani-Vazirani 2007. Curated by the 2026-06-28 source-grounded coverage pass. Dashboard-seeded keys were checked against the source inventory reports/source text when available; explicitly missing named source items are recorded as out_of_scope rather than silently omitted.

paperSlotsPerPageDistinct_iff.statement: - Paper multiple-slot distinctness spelled out by original query and slot.

paperSpend_formula.statement: - Paper spend formula for advertiser `a` under assignment `A`.

paperRevenue_formula.statement: - Paper revenue formula for an assignment.

paperFeasible_iff.statement: - Paper budget feasibility: no advertiser spends more than her budget.

paperSmallBids_iff.statement: - Paper small-bids condition: every bid is at most an `epsilon` budget fraction.

paperTradeoff_formula.statement: - The paper's MSVV/Balance tradeoff function at spent fraction `s`.

paperCanAssign_iff.statement: - Paper feasibility for assigning query `q` next to advertiser `a`.

paperIsBalanceChoice_iff.statement:
-
Paper Balance/MSVV choice rule: advertiser `a` is feasible for query `q` and
maximizes the scaled bid among feasible advertisers.

paperSmallBidsLimitFamily_fields.statement:
-
Paper-facing small-bids limiting family: bids become small relative to budgets,
offline optimum converges to `optLimit`, and Balance/MSVV revenue converges to
`revenueLimit`.
paperSmallBidsLimitFamily_fields.source_location: formalization bridge for Theorem 8 limiting statement

section6_different_budgets_and_nonexhaus.statement:
-
Section 6 items 1--2. Different advertiser budgets and nonexhaustive optima are
already part of the base AdWords model, so the finite explicit Theorem 8
guarantee applies without changing the instance.
section6_different_budgets_and_nonexhaus.source_location: paper-facing review target; exact source location to be refined

section6_next_highest_bid_all_formula.statement:
-
The all-bidders Section 6 next-price charge is the maximum of zero and the
largest bid from an advertiser other than `a`, or zero when there is no other
advertiser.

section6_next_highest_bid_alive_formula.statement:
-
The alive-bidders Section 6 next-price charge is the maximum of zero and the
largest bid from an alive advertiser other than `a`, or zero when no such
advertiser exists.

section6_page_top_balance_theorem8_finit.statement:
-
Section 6 multiple slots: source-shaped page-level finite explicit Theorem 8
guarantee. On each page `q`, Balance chooses the top `slots q` distinct feasible
advertisers by current scaled bid, and competes with the page-level offline
optimum subject to the same per-page cardinality and advertiser-budget
constraints.

section4_lemma1_balance_pays_no_later_sl.statement: - Section 4 Lemma 1: in the equal-bids Balance case, if OPT's bidder is still active in a no-later slab, Balance pays no later than the OPT type.

section4_lemma2_factor_revealing_lp_cons.statement: - Section 4 Lemma 2: Lemma 1's prefix accounting yields the factor-revealing LP row constraint.

section4_lemma3_factor_revealing_lp_opti.statement: - Section 4 Lemma 3: the displayed primal and dual factor-revealing LP witnesses give the limiting value N/e.

section5_lemma4_dual_optimal_from_primal.statement: - Section 5 Lemma 4: matching feasible primal and dual objectives certify optimality for the tradeoff-revealing LP.

section5_lemma5_tradeoff_rhs_eq_base_add.statement: - Section 5 Lemma 5: the perturbed tradeoff-revealing LP right-hand side equals the base LP right-hand side plus the paper delta term.

section5_lemma6_per_query_tradeoff.statement: - Section 5 Lemma 6: each query satisfies the pointwise tradeoff inequality used in the perturbation argument.

section5_lemma7_weighted_perturbation_bo.statement: - Section 5 Lemma 7: summing the pointwise tradeoff inequalities yields the weighted perturbation bound, including the paper-shaped N/k form.
